surfaces.part: main lower-left boulder, large white top

answer.evidence: The crag is a stack of boulders. The main lower-left boulder has a white top band on rows 30-37 (x=8). A darker edge line at row 29 sits above the band and another at row 38 closes it. A grey front face of about 4 rows (39-42) hangs below it. At x=15 the front is darker, rows 37-43. The upper boulders repeat this pattern: pale top bands at rows 3-5, 13-15 and 21-22, each followed by an edge line (rows 6, 16, 19/23) and grey faces below. The dark right-hand column (x=21, rows 20-41) is shading on the south face, not a receding side face. The object has horizontal top planes and a front face, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey rock pile (crag), not a tree, so the tree references are only a loose match for kind. Judged on craft alone, it still falls short. The candidate does not match the richness of the Beodeul reference trees, which carry leaf clumps and bark grain.
